text: MDM programs get funded because bad master data is already costing the business in ways people can point to — not because the topic is interesting on its own.

Duplicate outreach, mailing the same customer three times. Mismatched records that block automation, forcing someone to resolve them by hand forever. Inconsistent reporting, where two departments can't even agree on revenue per customer, so leadership stops trusting either number.

A single trusted view of the customer is the pitch that lands broadest. Mergers and acquisitions almost always force two separate customer and product sets together. Regulatory pressure often requires a de-duplicated view just to demonstrate compliance.

Before: three customer records, three different phone numbers, nobody sure which is current. After: one golden record — the subject of Chapter 2 — built by matching and merging those three down to one trusted answer.
Next: MDM governance — the roles and policies that keep a program like this from drifting back into chaos once it's funded and running.
